c: Loom & Lantern, a chain of craft and hobby stores
s: Loom & Lantern has 600 stores and an aging customer base. The director of marketing wants to attract younger customers through a campaign that encourages people to share what they make.
The director of marketing (judge) wants you to explain a campaign idea that builds buzz, how to use user-generated content, and how to keep the brand voice consistent on social media.
p: Explain the nature of buzz-marketing
Monitor user-generated content (UGC)
Maintain a consistent brand voice in social content
Explain the use of video/images for digital marketing
Explain the nature of corporate branding
n: Creates a hashtag or challenge that makes sharing fun
Monitors, reposts and responds to customer posts
Keeps the same tone, colors and style in every post
Uses short video and photo tutorials
Ties the idea to the brand promise: creativity and community
q: What would you do if a customer's post about your product went viral for the wrong reason?
How would you measure the success of the campaign?

c: Bloom Beauty, an online cosmetics brand
s: Bloom Beauty spends a large share of its budget on online ads and email, but cannot say which efforts bring in sales. The chief marketing officer wants to know what works.
The chief marketing officer (judge) wants you to explain how to track marketing communications, which measures matter and how to use data to make campaigns more relevant.
p: Identify ways to track marketing-communications activities
Use analytical tracking tools
Display data in charts/graphs or in tables
Leverage data to recommend personalized, relevant campaigns
Interpret statistical findings
n: Unique links, promo codes, pixels and dashboards
Reports on click-through, conversion, cost per sale and return on investment
Visuals that make results easy to compare
Segments customers by behavior and tailors email and ads
Looks for trends and avoids drawing conclusions from small samples
q: If an ad gets many clicks but few sales, what would you check?
How would you decide where to move budget if one channel performs better?

c: Peak Performance Gear, a maker of outdoor apparel
s: Peak Performance Gear is launching a new rain jacket and wants a content plan that reaches hikers, runners and commuters. The team has produced a lot of content but each platform looks and sounds different.
The marketing manager (judge) wants you to explain how to develop and repurpose content across platforms, how to write effective copy and how to coordinate the launch.
p: Repurpose content for use in multiple platforms
Write content for use in social media
Explain the use of storytelling in marketing
Explain the nature of a promotional plan
Execute targeted emails
n: Turns one video into short clips, stills, captions and blog excerpts
Writes concise, active copy that fits each platform
Uses a customer story to show the jacket in real conditions
Schedules teasers, launch and follow-up
Segments email lists by interest and sends relevant messages
q: How would you make sure the message is consistent across all platforms?
What would you do if an influencer partner posted inaccurate information about the jacket?

c: Spark Games, a video game publisher
s: Spark Games' online community is active but increasingly negative after a buggy release. Some players are posting insults and the company's responses have been slow and inconsistent.
The head of community (judge) wants you to explain how to moderate and engage the community, how to respond to complaints, and how to turn upset players into advocates.
p: Moderate social chats
Leverage social networks for customer engagement
Handle customer/client complaints
Describe considerations in developing customer evangelists
Explain the role of ethics in customer relationship management
n: Clear rules, quick removal of abusive content and consistent enforcement
Responds publicly with empathy, then solves privately
Acknowledges bugs, shares progress and rewards helpful players
Honest communication and no deleting legitimate criticism
q: A popular player posts false claims about your game. What do you do?
How do you respond to criticism when the team has not yet fixed the problem?

s: Horizon Credit Union is adding new employees to its marketing communications team. The communications director says successful specialists know how to write for different audiences, work with agencies and keep up with changing technology.
The communications director (judge) is interviewing you and wants you to explain what skills you would bring, how you would work with an outside agency, and how you would keep learning.
p: Explain the nature of marketing management
Create written briefs for outside agencies/consultants
Explain the use of advertising agencies
Explain the need for ongoing education as a worker
Adapt written correspondence to targeted audiences
n: Describes planning, coordinating and measuring communication activities
Writes a brief with objectives, audience, message, budget and timeline
Explains when an agency adds value and how to manage it
Follows trends through courses, industry groups and testing new tools
Changes tone for members, businesses and community partners
q: An agency delivers a design that does not match your brief. What do you do?
How would you explain a complex financial product to a first-time member?
